clue.text: Stone excluded from formal attitude in part of bridge

indicators.note: the stone abbreviation is shut out of the longer word, so it is removed

parts.note: starch is stiff formality of manner
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A mason leaves one stone out of the stiff formal pose of a bridge's structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge's span rests on curved supports, each one such a structural element.

clue.text: Bill exploited potential criminal

parts.note: ACC, short for account, is a bill
used means exploited, taken advantage of

explanation.surface: A man named Bill took advantage of someone who might turn to crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name but gives ACC, an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone charged but not yet convicted is only a possible wrongdoer until the trial ends.

clue.text: Kitchen container used in South American country for pepper

indicators.note: the container is placed within the country's name

parts.note: Chile is the country on South America's Pacific coast
a pot is a cooking vessel in the kitchen

explanation.surface: Cooking utensils in South America and a hot ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipotle is a smoke-dried jalapeño, a kind of chilli.

clue.text: Information not initially supplied in religious book

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: facts are information

explanation.surface: Details missing from the start of a book of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acts of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Secret letter she destroyed in Durham town

indicators.note: the letters of these three words are wrecked and rebuilt in new order

explanation.surface: Someone burns a confidential letter in a town in County Durham.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester-le-Street is a market town in County Durham, north-east England.

clue.text: Definite cut, over and over again — no end of trouble on the quiet

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: sure means definite

indicators.note: the letter that follows is taken away from the long synonym

parts.note: repetitiously means over and over again

indicators.note: the last letter of trouble is the one meant

explanation.surface: A sure reduction, repeated endlessly, keeps trouble quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims SURE to SUR; 'no end of trouble' removes an E from REPETITIOUSLY, leaving REPTITIOUSLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something stealthily is doing it secretly, without others noticing.

clue.text: Peace rather requiring a couple to reverse positions?

indicators.text: requiring a couple to reverse positions
indicators.note: two letters of the synonym swap places with each other

parts.note: quite means rather, as in quite good

explanation.surface: A rather peaceful scene where two people must swap places.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two letters, T and E, change places.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace and stillness are both a state free from noise or disturbance.

clue.text: Lit out from top-class landing-place

indicators.note: the three letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: quality as an adjective means top-class, as in a quality newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone leaves an excellent landing stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lit out' looks like slang for running off, but LIT is taken out of QUALITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A wharf or jetty is where boats land and unload.

clue.text: No opening to suggest some light work should arrive here

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to hint is to suggest
a ray is a beam, some light

explanation.surface: A boss suggests some light duties will come your way.
explanation.definitionFit: An office tray collects incoming papers and tasks awaiting attention.

clue.text: Left in care of those people and a woman

indicators.note: the letter is held inside the pronoun, as if looked after by it

parts.note: them refers to those people

explanation.surface: A child left in the care of a family and a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Showing less ardour, dismissing loves? Hold on

indicators.note: the two zero letters are sent away from the longer word

parts.note: cooling means becoming less passionate
love is zero in tennis, so two loves are two O letters

explanation.surface: A cooling lover, discarding affection, is told to hang on.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip tightly and refuse to let go of something is the sense here.

clue.text: Republicans wrecked club — I tell everyone

parts.note: GOP, the Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party

indicators.note: the letters of club and I are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A confession that Republicans trashed a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something public knowledge means disclosing it to all.

clue.text: Hear tune playing after pinning down unknown opera

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold the unknown letter inside them
the letters are performed in a different order

parts.note: Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Listen to music played once you've identified an obscure opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges HEAR TUNE into EURANTHE; 'pinning down' puts Y inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Euryanthe is an opera by Carl Maria von Weber, first staged in 1823.

clue.text: Athlete in useless club?

parts.note: shot can mean worn out or ruined, as in my nerves are shot
a putter is a golf club

explanation.surface: A sportsman's broken golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A field-event competitor hurls a heavy metal ball for distance.

clue.text: Contrary view of river entering Lake Placid

indicators.note: the stated containment is turned round, so the lake goes into the river instead
one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: Seen the other way, a river flows into Lake Placid in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Placid is a real US resort, which hides 'Placid' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid and tranquil both describe something still and untroubled.

clue.text: US author against one channel containing name

parts.note: V, for versus, means against

indicators.note: the name abbreviation sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: a gut is a narrow channel or strait

explanation.surface: An American writer opposing a single TV channel with a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Kurt Vonnegut was an American novelist, author of Slaughterhouse-Five.

clue.text: Consideration of French Revolution's aim?

parts.note: de is French for of
freedom was a goal of the French Revolution, as in liberty

explanation.surface: A historian weighs the goals of the French Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful thought or weighing up of a matter is consideration.

clue.text: Dog articles about wagging tails

indicators.note: the articles surround the shuffled letters

parts.note: a and an are the indefinite articles

indicators.note: a wagging tail moves about, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A dog whose tails are wagging, as described in some newspaper pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is another name for the German shepherd dog.

clue.text: Sorts out nets and dealings that may be confused

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Someone untangles fishing nets and muddled business affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Untangling or unravelling something is to sort it out.

clue.text: Dexterity keeping both ends of line in view

indicators.note: the larger word holds the picked letters within it

parts.note: sight means view

indicators.note: the first and last letters of line

explanation.surface: Skill in keeping a line straight while it is in sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is manual skill or deftness.

clue.text: Support Councillor ahead of awkward deal

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes before the following piece
the letters of deal are put in an awkward order

explanation.surface: A local politician supports an awkward deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cradle is a framework that holds something up, a support.

clue.text: Swift river trapping doctor

indicators.note: the river's name holds the doctor's letters inside

parts.note: the Nile is the river of Egypt
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A fast river current traps a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick and agile movement is swift.

clue.text: Journal mostly backing military action?

indicators.note: going backwards, the letters are read in reverse
the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a diary is a journal

explanation.surface: A war diary mostly supports a military operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims DIARY to DIAR, which 'backing' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden armed attack on an enemy position is an example of military action.

clue.text: Good to tuck into powerful beer — 9 on the scale?

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the phrase

parts.note: strong ale is a potent beer

explanation.surface: Drinkers tuck into potent beer, scoring nine out of ten.
explanation.walkthrough: The scale is the Beaufort wind scale, not a marking scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Force 9 on the Beaufort wind scale is named this, a severe wind.

clue.text: Crafty group of women meeting leading couple from Lysistrata

indicators.note: the two pieces join side by side

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation

indicators.note: the first two letters of the play's title

explanation.surface: A clever women's club reading Aristophanes' play about women.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cunning or sly means being crafty.

clue.text: University book left in cafes — one by Joyce?

indicators.note: the three letters are placed inside the synonym

parts.note: diners are cheap cafes

explanation.surface: A student leaves a book in a cafe: perhaps one by James Joyce?
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce's 1914 short-story collection; also, cryptically, any native of the Irish capital, as Joyce was.

clue.text: Slender drawing ultimately the hand of Addams?

parts.note: thin means slender

indicators.note: the last letter of drawing

explanation.surface: A thin cartoon line by Charles Addams, the cartoonist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand' seems to mean his drawing style, but means the disembodied hand in The Addams Family.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Addams Family, a disembodied hand is a household member with this name.

clue.text: English absolutely the best possible

parts.note: very, as in the very best, means absolutely

explanation.surface: English is absolutely top-notch.
explanation.definitionFit: In phrases like every chance of success, the word means all possible, the greatest possible.

clue.text: Lead ingredients in ten of your sherry trifles

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next four words are taken

explanation.surface: A cook adds the key ingredients to ten sherry trifles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifles' looks like the dessert but means playthings.
explanation.definitionFit: Toys and trifles are both things of little importance or playthings.

clue.text: Seabird whose sound is viewed negatively?

indicators.note: the bird's name said out loud gives the word that follows

parts.note: not is the word of negation

explanation.surface: A seabird's call is not well received.
explanation.definitionFit: The knot is a wading shore bird, a sandpiper of coasts and estuaries.
